result.rationale: In the Google CalendarService, the fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is only evaluated in the ternary's else branch, i.e., when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. The predicate then compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` where externalCalendarId is null/undefined/empty, so the find never matches and the fallback always yields undefined (falling through to undefined/primary). Same dead logic appears in updateEvent and deleteEvent. This is a real defect introduced by the diff.

judged_text: Fallback find by externalCalendarId only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, so the find predicate compares against undefined and never matches, breaking the calendar id fallback (CalendarService.ts:253-256, 312-315)

record.issue_text: Fallback find by externalCalendarId only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, so the find predicate compares against undefined and never matches, breaking the calendar id fallback (CalendarService.ts:253-256, 312-315)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `updateEvent` computes `selectedCalendar` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` (similarly in `deleteEvent` for `calendarId`). The `find(...)` branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the predicate compares `cal.externalId` against the same falsy value (`undefined`/`null`). That will almost never match a real calendar externalId, so the fallback effectively returns `undefined` and breaks selecting a destination calendar when no `externalCalendarId` is provided.
